title: The make-up Lamare band and the close of the interview
summary: A band of youngsters including Hilton Lamare; interviewers end the session.

story.theme_name: Thanks and goodbyes: closing the interview
story.community_name: Closing thanks and goodbyes at the end of the interview

blocks.x: What about Le Maire? You were telling me about helping Le Maire's band. I never did get that straight. It was in there.

Well, it was a make-up band. We were all youngsters and we, I don't know who got the job, whether, I got it or I think it was Durfie's job. It was Durfie's brother's. One played drum, one played clarinder. Hilton played panjo. No, one played saxophone. That's it, alto sax. And, uh, Bouchon played clarinder. It was a five or six piece congo. All youngsters. Hilton's about my age, about 54. He's got a brother, too, plays music. Jimmy Lamar. Did you know him? Piano player? No, I've seen his- No, saxophone. Yeah.

No. But Eddie Lamar played piano. I don't know Eddie. Don't keep them all straight. Some days you just can't think. That's what I get for staying up so late at night. I guess we better call it to a halt. Thank you.
